ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure is a switching converter, containing an input source Vin, an inductor L, a switch S, a diode, and the output-side capacitor C and resistor R; the reference polarity of the inductor voltage VL is marked as left positive and right negative. The right side gives the periodic waveform of VL: within one switching period Ts, VL is first +15 V, then -45 V, and repeats periodically. Reasoning: According to the specified method, let the conduction duty ratio of switch S be D, that is, the S conduction time is D Ts. From the corresponding relationship of the circuit operating states, when S is on, VL = +15 V, and when S is off, VL = -45 V. In steady state and when the inductor current is continuous, the inductor volt-second balance holds, so 15(DTs) + (-45)((1-D)Ts) = 0. Eliminating Ts gives 15D - 45 + 45D = 0, namely 60D = 45, therefore D = 0.75.

method.method_draft: Let D be the fraction of Ts for which switch S is ON. From the circuit, associate the ON interval with VL = +15 V and the OFF interval with VL = −45 V. Apply volt-second balance: 15(DTs) + (−45)((1−D)Ts) = 0. Cancel Ts and solve 15D − 45 + 45D = 0, so 60D = 45 and D = 0.75.

method.method_draft: Use the waveform levels to determine the converter voltages. Since the ON-state VL equals Vin, Vin = 15 V. In the OFF state, VL = Vin − Vo = −45 V, so Vo = 15 + 45 = 60 V. Apply the ideal CCM boost relation Vo = Vin/(1−D): 60 = 15/(1−D). Thus 1−D = 0.25 and D = 0.75.
